title: Disabilities, Adaptations & Test Support
whatItIs: Candidates should declare a disability when booking. They drive to the same standard to pass, but the examiner adapts and can restrict the licence to adapted cars.
keyFacts: Examiners ask about adaptations and how they work, and complete form D255, pass or fail.
If the pupil can only drive with adaptations, restriction codes go on the pass certificate.
With a code on the licence, driving without that adaptation breaks the law.
Deaf candidates: written notes at the start, directions usually by hand signals.
Electric and semi-automatic cars count as automatics for test and licence.

points: The driver needs automatic gear selection because of a disability
A restriction linked to the disability

onTheTest.question: A disabled pupil passes their test in a car with a hand-operated brake and accelerator. What happens to the pass?
options: A normal pass, with no restrictions
No pass until they test in an unadapted car
A pass for automatic cars only
Restriction codes for the adaptations go on the pass certificate
onTheTest.why: DT1 8.05: if the examiner considers the candidate can only drive a vehicle with suitable adaptations, the restriction code is entered on the pass certificate (DVSA10).

onTheTest.question: A deaf pupil wants a British Sign Language interpreter on their car test. What is correct?
options: They must be at least 16 and can be the pupil's ADI
DVSA provides and pays for the interpreter
Interpreters are not allowed on the car test
They must be at least 21 and hold a full licence
onTheTest.why: A BSL interpreter must be at least 16 and the driving instructor can be the interpreter. The candidate arranges and pays, and can claim the cost back.

traps: Foreign language interpreters are not allowed on test; special needs interpreters for deaf candidates are.
Being very tall or very short is not in itself a disability: no restriction and no D255.
Pregnant candidates can test at any stage, but must be able and willing to do an emergency stop.
Left-foot braking in an automatic is only a fault if the footbrake is used against the accelerator.
